title: Storage planes
preamble:
# Storage planes

The three storage planes DS rules interact with: **facts**,
**samples**, and **cache**. This document describes only the
author-visible surface and the semantic
guarantees the language relies on. Backend choices, wire
protocols, connection topology, queueing, federation, and
deployment shape are runtime concerns, out of scope.

Paired with:
- [LGRA.10] — the action grammar for
  `cache`, `cached(...)`, `cache_delete`, and the `call storage;*`
  service-invocation form.
- [LSER] — series declarations; the `persist:`
  kwarg there is the author-facing samples-write knob.
- [LLOG] and
  [LFAC] — fact lifecycle, orthogonal
  to persistence.

## What this is not

- Not an implementation spec. Backends (append-only log,
  TSDB, in-memory KV), wire protocols, queueing policies,
  shedding mechanisms, federation, and deployment shape
  belong with the runtime that hosts the storage adapter.
- Not an SQL / external-query surface. External consumers
  (dashboards, ad-hoc queries) talk to backends directly;
  DS rule-facing access goes through the typed primitives
  below.
